inspection.result: The broad harmonic comb, descending second-vowel pitch, and substantial upper texture are already visible at the coupled glottal source. inspection.result: Two vowels, descending harmonic comb, near-horizontal upper bands and ringing remain visibly similar to baseline at the same gain and color scale. Removing stochastic aspiration/frication pressures did not remove the targeted visual pattern. This does not establish perceptual equivalence or eliminate all randomness: jitter and shimmer remain.
inspection.next_experiment: Change only the baseline contact_softness from 3e-8 to 3e-7 m2, retaining baseline turbulence. Test sensitivity to near-seal aperture rounding without filtering output or promoting the setting.

playback.processing: one fixed gain over the full recording; no cuts or filters

inspection.result: Full 684 x 567 field inspected at original magma scale. Much of the dense upper-frequency texture is reduced, especially the region above the main lower vowel bands; both voiced regions, lower harmonic structure and descending pitch remain. Narrow resonance ridges persist. Together with the rounded source-derivative trace and the near-unchanged no-turbulence field, this supports a contact-related contribution to the upper texture, not a proven cure of perceived mechanical timbre.
inspection.next_investigation: Relate near-seal airflow to actual distributed fold contact geometry and consistent force/flow area. Keep the accepted default unchanged; do not treat the diagnostic 10x area scale as measured anatomy.
